notes: Spec asserts: ready → working → ready when the user cancels a long turn with ESC (state does not stick in working post-interrupt), then a second clean ready → working → ready arc proves the parser reset. muse is a single-birth FilesUnderRoot adapter (session id = directory basename), so birth anchors to "start" unpinned. The interrupted turn's prompt asks muse to run a real `sleep 45` shell command via its bash/execute tool, deliberately un-completable within interrupt_to_ready's max_delay_ms bound — this is the vacuous-pass guard: unlike claudecode's 'long essay' template, a natural completion literally cannot satisfy this phase, so a silently no-op interrupt driver step would time out rather than pass. turn_start anchors to session_birth (event.kind:"started", EventType=user_message); interrupt_to_ready anchors to turn_start on the run's own terminal:"cancelled" record (EventType=turn_done, parser.go parseRunTerminal — muse's parser sets turn_done uniformly for completed/cancelled, so this arc is produced by the SAME code path as ordinary completion, independent of IsUserInterrupt; see the cell's caveats for the adapter-side labeling gap that leaves). turn2_start/turn2_end assert the clean post-interrupt reset via a NEW run_id. All non-birth phases pin same_session_as:session_birth — muse spawns reminder subagents freely (their own working→ready arcs must not satisfy a parent-session phase). Session-birth/pid-bind timing bounds and the interrupt_to_ready bound are estimates from a live tmux/ESC probe done for this assessment (not yet a recorded irrlichd observation) — see the assessment's caveats. CORRECTED post-record (2026-09-15, live recording): dropped the teardown/process_exited phase, mirroring 2-13_turn-end-terminal-text/2-15_shell-escape-command/2-16_oversized-transcript-line's precedent — the recorded process_exited landed on a reminder-subagent session (6a682f64-c07d-497b-832f-e94c6740f9a9), never on the parent session (01a0a216-cec2-74f1-8796-c7031014c40c), reproducing the OPEN daemon bug ingo-eichhorst/Irrlicht#1962 (processlifecycle's per-PID watched map is last-write-wins; one muse process serves the parent and every reminder child, so a single process_exited lands on whichever session registered last). All 6 remaining phases passed cleanly on this recording, including the load-bearing interrupt_to_ready phase (matched at +5894ms, well under the 20000ms bound and the sleep 45 command's own floor) and confirmed the assessment's main-session discriminator live: the interrupted run's own goal_usage_attribution record carries owner.requester_kind:"main", owner.owner_type:"main_root" (run_id 77c4db9e-3950-48e2-84c4-4be4e2fb431f), matching the cell's live-probe evidence exactly.

text: Session appears in ready shortly after the muse TUI finishes launching
muse-bin PID bound to the session via its .session.lock held flock fd
First user prompt (run a `sleep 45` shell command) drives ready → working

ESC pressed mid-turn cancels the run (run.terminal terminal:"cancelled" → turn_done → ready); the 20s bound is well under the sleep command's own 45s floor, so this transition can only be a genuine interrupt, not a natural completion
Second, short prompt ("Reply with exactly the word: RECOVERED") drives ready → working again on a NEW run — proving the parser did not stick on any interrupt-related state
Second turn completes normally (run.terminal terminal:"completed" → turn_done) → ready — the clean post-interrupt arc
